faq.q: How much can rent be increased in BC in 2026?
faq.a: Up to 2.3% for a residential tenancy (the published 2027 limit is 2.2%), only once every 12 months, on at least 3 full months' written notice on form RTB-7; anything above the limit needs an RTB-52 arbitrator application or the tenant's voluntary written agreement (RTB Rent increases page, as cited on the live page).

faq.q: Can a landlord end a tenancy because the property is being sold?
faq.a: No: the tenancy continues and the buyer becomes the new landlord. Only once all conditions of sale are met can a purchaser who intends to live in the unit (or have a close family member live there) ask the seller in writing to give a Three Month Notice (RTB-32P), which must be generated through the RTB web portal (RTB Sell a rental property page, as cited on the live page).

faq.q: What form starts a tenancy, and when must the tenant get a copy?
faq.a: Form RTB-1, the Residential Tenancy Agreement — or an equivalent agreement containing all the standard terms the Residential Tenancy Act requires. The landlord must give the tenant a copy within 21 days of signing (RTB Tenancy agreements page, as cited on the live page).
